solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A purist's worked out on the first floor?

indicators.note: a puzzle worked out is solved, its pieces put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somebody who insists on doing things properly has been exercising in a room above ground level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' reads as exercise, but it signals rearranging the letters of A PURIST'S.
explanation.definitionFit: The first floor in Britain is the storey above the ground floor, reached by going up the stairs.

clue.text: Resolved gripe about shameful unfair advantage

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
something resolved has been sorted out, so the letters of gripe are rearranged

parts.note: shameful means vile, contemptible

explanation.surface: A complaint has been settled concerning a disgraceful, unfair edge someone enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' reads as 'settled' but signals the anagram, PRIGE; 'about' wraps those letters round the synonym for shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special right or benefit enjoyed by some and not others, hence an unearned edge.

clue.text: Cree petitioner carries up old shelter?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the words Cree petitioner carry the letters within them, spanning the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A member of the Cree nation making a petition hauls something up an incline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' takes EEPET from inside 'Cree petitioner'; 'up' reads it bottom to top in this down entry. The Cree setting fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A conical tent of skins once used by Plains peoples of North America; the question mark admits it is a loose description.

clue.text: Instigate one new church feature

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a spire is the tapering tower on top of a church

explanation.surface: Start off by installing one fresh addition to a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to prompt or stir up action, which is to stimulate or motivate it.

clue.text: Put money aside to acquire old Italian wine

indicators.note: the saving piece acquires, takes into itself, the next letter

parts.note: to put money aside is to save

explanation.surface: Somebody saves up in order to buy a vintage bottle from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white made around the town of that name near Verona.

clue.text: Small fuss over drink

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for fuss is read backwards

parts.note: ado is fuss, bother

explanation.surface: A minor commotion breaks out over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy water or a sweet carbonated soft drink, an example of something to drink.

clue.text: Ultimately vacuous glib talk in splash

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the next word, its final letter

parts.note: patter is the fast smooth talk of a salesman or comedian

explanation.surface: Empty, slick chatter ends up as nothing more than a splash.
explanation.definitionFit: To spatter is to splash in drops, a synonym as verb or noun.

clue.text: Party supported by English female

indicators.note: in a down entry, being supported by means sitting on top of the next piece

parts.note: a do is a party or social gathering

explanation.surface: A political party relies on an English woman for backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A doe is the female of deer, rabbits and similar animals.

clue.text: Ineffective person with island politician

parts.note: I is the standard abbreviation for island, as on maps
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A useless individual accompanies an island's member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeble, timid person lacking courage is a weakling, the slang sense here.

clue.text: Sailor, southeastern, at a distance, I hesitate to say

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast
afar means far away
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone cautiously describes a mariner who is far away to the southeast.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer is someone who travels by sea, a mariner.

clue.text: If coming back, dwell where it's warm

indicators.note: coming back means the word If is written backwards

parts.note: to reside is to live or dwell

explanation.surface: If you return, you can live somewhere warm.
explanation.definitionFit: The area beside a fire in a home is the cosy spot for warming up.

clue.text: Cutting pastry

definitions.meaning: cutting remarks are sharp, acid or sour
a pastry case with a sweet filling, such as jam or fruit

explanation.surface: Slicing a baked dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart means sharp-tongued as an adjective and is also a kind of open pie.

clue.text: Ask further questions about old article on pit

parts.note: re means about, concerning
ex means former, old
a is the indefinite article
a mine is a pit dug for coal or ore

explanation.surface: An item concerning an old colliery invites further investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' simply puts the earlier pieces above MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine again, as a lawyer does a witness after cross-questioning, is to question once more.

clue.text: Replace pro? Ire develops in vehicle

indicators.note: something that develops changes its form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A professional is being substituted, and anger grows in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develops' rearranges the thirteen letters of REPLACE, PRO and IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A people carrier is a British name for a minivan, a large car built for many passengers.

clue.text: I entered into clear understanding

indicators.note: the letter I is entered into the word for clear

parts.note: patent means plain, obvious, clear

explanation.surface: Someone joins a mutual agreement that is clearly set out.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient person is tolerant and forbearing, which is what understanding means as an adjective.

clue.text: Some fly-half, redoubtable Spaniard perhaps

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rugby fly-half, a formidable player, is perhaps from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: A fly-half is a rugby position.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfredo is a common Spanish man's name, so a Spaniard is a likely bearer of it.

clue.text: Advanced just before Easter

definitions.meaning: advanced as in money handed over on loan
the Christian season of fasting in the forty days before Easter

explanation.surface: Something moved forward shortly ahead of the Easter holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Lent is the past tense of lend, meaning advanced as a loan, and the penitential season preceding Easter.

clue.text: Flatter senior citizen after newspaper in call for help

indicators.note: after puts the senior citizen behind the other pieces
in means the newspaper goes inside the distress call

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
OAP is an old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: A pensioner sweet-talks after reading the paper and then cries for help.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP (old-age pensioner) and FT (Financial Times) are British abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-soap someone is to persuade them with flattery, an idiom for cajoling.

clue.text: Evidence of damage on female neckwear

parts.note: a scar is a mark left by an injury

explanation.surface: A woman's neck covering shows signs of having been damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarf is a strip of fabric worn round the neck for warmth or style.

clue.text: He's sinful, awfully tempting and nefarious first of all?

definitions.text: He's sinful, awfully tempting and nefarious first of all?

indicators.note: first of all takes the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A description of a wicked, seductive and villainous person.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both describes the Devil and spells him out with the initials of 'sinful, awfully, tempting and nefarious'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil is the arch-tempter of scripture, wicked and tempting by nature.

clue.text: Cheapest tickets were here in the main

definitions.text: Cheapest tickets were here in the main

parts.words: Cheapest tickets were here in the main
parts.note: the main is the sea; on an ocean liner the lowest fare bought space in the poorest accommodation

explanation.surface: Mostly, the lowest-priced seats were in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly' but means at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: On passenger ships, the lowest class of travel, below decks, was the cheapest berth.

clue.text: Number brunette's holding up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the word brunette's holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: A figure that the dark-haired woman is holding aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten is a cardinal number, one more than nine.

clue.text: Get tree branch

definitions.meaning: to get it is to understand, catch on
a small slender shoot of a tree

explanation.surface: Fetch a bough from a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Twig is informal British for understand, and also a small branch.

clue.text: Regularly consult old King

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the next word, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Seek advice often from an elderly monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cnut, or Canute, was an eleventh-century ruler of England, Denmark and Norway.

clue.text: Fish move with difficulty

definitions.meaning: a flatfish such as a plaice or fluke
to struggle clumsily, as through mud or water

explanation.surface: A sea creature struggling along.
explanation.definitionFit: Flounder names a flatfish and also means to stagger or struggle awkwardly.
